summary: New OBS overlay: show the timer on your recording.
bullets: New overlay page that shows the current block and countdown and follows the timer page live. Add it to OBS as a Browser Source, with a transparent background that scales to the size you give it
Click the OBS icon at the right of the top bar for setup instructions and a Copy URL button
To use it, open Bailiff in OBS as a Custom Browser Dock (Docks > Custom Browser Docks) and add the overlay address as a Browser Source. Both must load from the same web address

Change the size of the block name, countdown, time label and pause timer, and pick the color of each one (including the countdown's last 30 seconds, last 10 seconds and overtime, and paused colors) with a color picker that matches the site. Changes show on the overlay immediately
The overlay uses light colors with a soft shadow by default so it reads over video, and the pause timer is hidden unless you turn it on
Fixed: the saved trials list could show a long decimal for the time on a trial that was paused or stopped mid-second (like 26:7.9090000000001055). It now shows whole seconds

summary: Major update: a new Timeline tab for logging everything that happens in a round.
bullets: New Timeline tab on the timer page (switch between Timer and Timeline at the top). The timer keeps running while you're on it, and the current block and clock stay visible
Every start, pause and stop is logged automatically, with the time of day, trial time since the start time (once set), and the timer reading
Each pause is a single entry showing how long it lasted and how it ended: resumed, sustained (deducted) or overruled (deducted from the linked block)
Drop a flag at any moment without pausing, from the bench or the Timeline tab, with an optional quick note. Flags can be deleted
Add or edit a note on any entry, such as "hearsay objection" on a pause or flag
Entries are grouped under mini headings showing the side, team, block and witness. Sort oldest first or newest first, and hide flags with one checkbox
A filter menu lets you view just one side (all Plaintiff or all Defense), a whole block, or a single witness, with entry counts. On small screens it collapses behind a Filter button
The timeline is saved with the trial, autosave and page reloads, and is included in JSON and text exports and imports
New built-in preset: 2026 LHS Intramurals (VLRE with a 21:00 direct and 15:00 cross)
Fixed: stopping or pausing the timer no longer rounds the main countdown to the last whole second; it keeps the exact time
Fixed: the main button says Start, not Restart, for a block or witness that was never stopped (including after a reload or when moving to the next block)
The big countdown display on the timer page now ticks with millisecond precision instead of jumping once a second
Every other time display (widgets, secondary timer, block list) still shows whole seconds

summary: Control which case names show up as placeholder suggestions.
bullets: New pencil icon next to "In the Matter Of" opens a Case Name Suggestions manager
Enable or disable individual famous cases, with a search box and Enable All / Disable All (scoped to whatever the search currently shows)
Add your own custom cases, remove them individually, or Clear All (with a confirmation prompt)
Import or export custom cases as JSON, via file or clipboard
If nothing's enabled and there are no custom cases, the fields fall back to plain "Plaintiff" / "Defense" placeholders

summary: AMTA preset breaks Opening & Closing into segments.
bullets: The AMTA preset's Opening & Closing block now has individual segments per side (Opening Statement, Closing Argument, and Closing Rebuttal for Plaintiff) instead of one shared timer

summary: Track the trial clock, not just the block clocks.
bullets: New Trial Clock bar at the bottom of the timer page shows the current time and elapsed time since the trial started
Set the start time once (defaults to now, editable in the moment). after confirming, it locks in for the rest of the trial
Elapsed time turns red past 180 minutes, the AMTA all-loss-time threshold
Start time is saved with the session, so it survives autosave recovery and resuming a saved trial
New built-in AMTA preset, alongside VLRE

summary: Fix manual time controls not syncing the block total.
bullets: Adjusting a witness's time with the manual controls (+15/+30/-15/-30, custom Add/Set/Sub, Reset) now updates the block's real total right away, instead of only catching up once the clock ticks or a ruling deducts from it
In Total Time mode, granting time to a witness now actually adds to the case's real time remaining instead of just changing how much that witness appears to have used.
A hint now explains why the elapsed number above moves the opposite way

summary: Next Block now follows actual trial order.
bullets: Next Block used to run through one side's whole schedule before moving to the other. It now alternates sides at each step, including witness by witness within a block (Plaintiff Witness 1, Defense Witness 1, Plaintiff Witness 2...), before moving down to the next section, matching how a trial actually runs
The VLRE preset now includes witnesses for Cross Examination too, mirrored from Direct, and loads by default when you start a new setup
Renaming a witness now offers to rename same-named witnesses elsewhere (like their Cross Examination counterpart), showing which block each one is in
Allocated Time now warns before starting a trial if a block's Plaintiff and Defense witness totals don't match, so neither side gets shortchanged
Export a custom preset through the same dialog trials use. Copy it to your clipboard or download it as a file
Blocks like Direct and Cross can now have witnesses, each with its own timer
Choose Allocated Time (each witness gets a set countdown) or Stopwatch (open-ended, just tracks elapsed) per block
Copy a block's witnesses into another block, handy for mirroring Direct's witness list onto Cross
The block itself always keeps its own real total, shown as a collapsible header above its witnesses on the timer page

summary: See how long each section actually ran.
bullets: Stopped blocks on the timer page now show an "Elapsed" time alongside the remaining/total display
Elapsed time turns red if a section ran past its allotted time

summary: Turn a saved trial into a shareable image.
bullets: New "Image" export format alongside Plain Text and JSON: a docket-style poster with the schedule and progress
Copy the image straight to your clipboard, or download it as a PNG

summary: Take your saved trials with you.
bullets: Export any saved trial as a readable summary or a JSON file
Copy an export to your clipboard, or download it as a file
Import trials from a JSON file: drag & drop it in, browse for it, or paste it directly
